text:
talia: deploybot flagged a p95 jump in canary after v3.6.0. autopilot stayed muted. can someone take ownership for a manual path?

owen: on it. looks like generator tail-latency +270ms in eu-central canary (slice=6%). no 5xxs.

ops-bot: snapshot: region=euc1 canary=6% p95_delta=+270ms error_rate=0.8% baseline=0.5% host_restart=0

lee: prefer a manual rollback. propose criteria: sustained >200ms for 4m AND operator handshake. prevents double actions.

talia: agreed. also we need a release-note blurb and a short customer line if we revert. @nora can you own comms?

nora: will draft. short message: "We reverted the most recent canary due to an observed latency regression; traffic restored to v3.5.3. We'll follow up with details and a patch plan."

owen: triage points to attention-kernel dispatch change in 3.6.0 under long-history prompts. reproducible on staging. ops, do you want kernel flag toggle or straight revert?

lee: revert to stable for now. command: `/release rollback --to v3.5.3 --operator lee --reason "canary p95 regression"`

talia: operator handshake: @lee you have go-ahead? @nora prepare comms. owen standby to capture logs.

lee: I confirm. executing in 15s.

deploybot: rollback request received. running prechecks...

deploybot: prechecks OK  artifact v3.5.3 verified, migrations=none, canary pool target reachable. starting rollback: canary -> demote -> full drain of v3.6.0. ETA ~3m.

deploybot: rollback complete. active=v3.5.3 inactive=v3.6.0 canary=0%

owen: verified p95 returned to baseline within 90s. opened REL-5599 for kernel regression.

nora: comms sent to #customer-success and drafted release notes line.

talia: thanks. post-rollback checklist: ops monitor 12h, owen+lee investigate kernel diff, nora finalize external note. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
